title: Type-1 first-period interest: four witnesses agreeing to ten decimal places
upstream_status_verbatim: **Pending**: live-Excel bit pinning of the type=1 witnesses on the probe lane
status_plain: The type-1 defect on IPMT, PPMT, CUMIPMT and CUMPRINC was verified against live Excel on build 20026 with four witnesses, and they agree -- but to TEN DECIMAL PLACES, not to bits. That predicate is neither of the two the evidence schema admits, so this record deliberately publishes NO COUNT rather than folding a tolerant comparison into either enum value. The source itself flags the gap: bit pinning of the type-1 witnesses is listed as pending, and the numeric closed-form pins use a tight tolerance while the exact publication bits remain to be pinned. A page that renders these four surfaces as bit-exact on the strength of this stream is quoting a tolerant comparison as an exact one.
open_question: The exact f64 publication bits for the type-1 witnesses are not pinned. The source: "- **Pending**: live-Excel bit pinning of the type=1 witnesses on the probe lane" and "(numeric closed-form pins use a tight tolerance; the exact f64 publication bits remain to be pinned)."
reader_warning: This record carries no count on purpose. The source's predicate is agreement "to 10 decimal places", which neither `exact-typed-bit-match` nor `15-significant-digit-truncation` describes, and inventing a fit for it would misrepresent the strength of the evidence. Four witnesses at a tolerant predicate is not a corpus and not a bit-exactness claim. The existing type=0 Excel-bit witnesses are a separate, stronger thing and are not counted here either.
